name: Predisposition to invasive fungal disease due to CARD9 deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the CARD9 gene by genetic testing
History of recurrent or persistent invasive fungal infections, especially candidiasis or dermatophytosis
Demonstration of impaired neutrophil or macrophage fungal killing or defective cytokine production in vitro

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic CARD9 variants plus clinical evidence of invasive fungal infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional immunological assays can support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent Candida infections of skin and mucous membranes
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

pathognomonic.notes: Invasive fungal infection of skin and subcutaneous tissues by dermatophytes

common.notes: Intracranial fungal infections causing abscess formation

common.symptomName: Chronic sinusitis due to fungal infection

occasional.notes: Bone infections secondary to fungal invasion
Enlarged lymph nodes due to fungal infection
searchTerms: lymph node swelling due to fungus

occasional.symptomName: Fever of unknown origin during fungal infection episodes

rare.notes: Infection of meninges by fungal organisms
Fungal abscess formation in liver and spleen
searchTerms: fungal abscesses in liver and spleen
fungal spots in liver and spleen

laboratory: Positive fungal cultures from sterile sites
Elevated inflammatory markers during infection episodes
Impaired cytokine production (e.g., IL-17, IL-22) in immune assays
imaging: MRI or CT evidence of fungal abscesses in brain, lungs, or bones
Echocardiography revealing fungal vegetations in endocarditis
other: Family history of invasive fungal infections

distinguishingFeatures: Usually associated with STAT1 gain-of-function mutations
Predominantly mucocutaneous involvement without deep invasive infections
Defect in NADPH oxidase complex leading to impaired respiratory burst
Recurrent bacterial and fungal infections including catalase-positive organisms

redFlags: Recurrent or persistent invasive fungal infections despite standard antifungal therapy
Early onset of deep dermatophytosis or fungal brain abscesses
Family history of severe fungal infections or consanguinity
references: Lanternier F, et al. CARD9 deficiency and invasive fungal infections: a review. Curr Opin Infect Dis. 2015;28(4):303-309.
Glocker EO, et al. CARD9 deficiency in humans causes susceptibility to fungal infections. Nature. 2009; 459(7245): 693-697.
Drummond RA, et al. CARD9-dependent neutrophil recruitment protects against fungal invasion of the central nervous system. PLoS Pathog. 2015;11(10):e1005293.
